body.statement: For every \((P,\Pi,T)\) in \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the law of \(O_{T,\Delta}\) equals the law obtained from two independent infinite arm tapes with respective marginals \((Y(a),D(a))\), where policy \(\Pi\) consumes the next unused entry of the assigned tape and reveals the record \((t,W_t,V_t,D_t(W_t),Y_t(W_t))\) at calendar time \(V_t\). Consequently, every deterministic prefix of each tape is an independent and identically distributed arm sample, unconditionally and without imposing independence between \(Y(a)\) and \(D(a)\).
body.justification: This observed-kernel equivalence is the device that converts arbitrary predictable allocation into deterministic independent arm prefixes.
body.gap: Adaptive AIPW proofs use martingale centering, while reward-dependent-delay lower bounds use tailored instances; neither supplies this unconditional observed-law reduction with delayed histories.
body.consumer: The reduction permits fixed-quota inference for any logged policy obeying the exploration envelope, including policies whose scaled propensities do not converge.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mu_a\) denote the marginal law of \((Y_t(a),D_t(a))\).  By ass:iid-arrivals, the current vector of potential outcome--delay pairs is independent of \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and has its common law.  By ass:sequential-randomization, conditional on \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), on \(W_t=a\), and on the current potential vector, the assignment contributes the predictable factor \(\pi_t(a)\).  Consequently, after integrating out the unassigned component, the conditional kernel for the newly consumed observed pair \(Z_t=(Y_t(W_t),D_t(W_t))\) is
\[
 P\{W_t=a,Z_t\in dz\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\}
 =\pi_t(a)\mu_a(dz).
\]
The revelation at \(t+D_t(W_t)\) is a deterministic measurable operation on \(t,W_t,Z_t\).  Thus, if \(h_{t-1}\) is any possible delayed observed history, the transition kernel from \(h_{t-1}\) first draws \(a\) with probabilities \(\pi_t(a;h_{t-1})\), then draws \(z\) from \(\mu_a\), and schedules the corresponding revelation.

Now put on an auxiliary space independent sequences \(\{Z_{a,j}:j\geq1\}\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), with \(Z_{a,j}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mu_a\), the two sequences being independent.  At assignment \(W_t=a\), consume \(Z_{a,N_a(t)}\).  Conditional on the delayed history and \(W_t=a\), that unused tape entry has law \(\mu_a\) and is independent of the history.  Hence this construction has exactly the transition kernel displayed above.  Induction on \(t=1,\ldots,T\) proves equality of all finite-dimensional laws of assignments, logged propensities, scheduled revelation times, and records revealed by every calendar time \(s\leq H_T\).  In particular it proves equality of the law of \(O_{T,\Delta}\).  Dependence between \((Y_t(0),D_t(0))\) and \((Y_t(1),D_t(1))\) causes no discrepancy: only one of those two components enters the displayed observed kernel.

Every deterministic prefix \((Z_{a,1},\ldots,Z_{a,K})\) is therefore an iid \(\mu_a\)-sample, and the two represented prefixes are independent.  This is an unconditional assertion; no event involving the calendar times at which the entries are consumed has been conditioned upon.

For the requested smallest adaptive stress test, take \(T=2\) and any finite-support \(\mu_0,\mu_1\).  Let the second assignment probability be one value when the first response has been revealed with positive sign, another when it has been revealed with nonpositive sign, and a third when it is still pending.  For \(a_1,a_2\in\mathcal A\) and tape values \(z_1,z_2\), both the arrival model and the tape model assign the cylinder the probability
\[
 \pi_1(a_1)\mu_{a_1}(z_1)
 \pi_2(a_2;h_1(a_1,z_1))\mu_{a_2}(z_2).
\]
The history \(h_1\) uses \(z_1\) only when its delay makes it observable.  The equality holds for every atom and uses no factorization of the outcome and delay within \(z_1\).  This verifies exactly that reward-dependent switching and informative delay do not invalidate the reduction.
